record_identity.title: GTG-27005 used Claude Code to develop and simulate an autonomous FPV kamikaze drone swarm

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Anthropic GTG-27005 / DronDoc / Serafim autonomous drone-swarm development
incident_identity.date_basis: Anthropic reports activity disrupted during the December 2025-August 2026 reporting period and describes GTG-27005 as a sustained operation. Independent reporting places the observed DronDoc work from mid-May 2026. The exact first and last dates of the GTG-27005 activity are not established in the reviewed primary disclosure, so the record conservatively bounds the evidenced 2026 activity to May-August 2026.

summary: Anthropic reports that likely freelance Russia-based threat actors used Claude Code as part of an effort to develop a full-stack autonomous first-person-view kamikaze drone swarm called DronDoc or Serafim. According to Anthropic, Claude was used to write and test project code for shared swarm memory, fault-tolerant coordination logic, an onboard small language model governing attack, observation and return-to-base behaviours, terminal guidance and detonation logic, control-link geolocation, passive acoustic detection and low-level programmable-chip logic. Anthropic assessed the resulting systems at Technology Readiness Level 3-4: validated in simulation, with code loaded onto real boards, but did not report an operational fielded swarm or casualties resulting from the system. Anthropic states that safeguards blocked many requests but not all, that the actors used concealment and session-splitting tactics to evade safeguards, and that associated accounts were disrupted.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Anthropic's September 2026 threat-intelligence report directly identifies GTG-27005, describes the actors as likely freelance and Russia-based, identifies Claude Code as a development tool, enumerates the software subsystems built with Claude assistance, and assesses the observed systems at TRL 3-4. The same report states that conventional-weapons actors used tactics including concealment and splitting work across sessions to evade safeguards, and that safeguards blocked many requests but not all. Anthropic's separate September 2026 conventional-weapons capability evaluation provides broader corroborating evidence that frontier models can materially assist tactical targeting and conventional-weapons engineering tasks, but it does not independently establish the GTG-27005 occurrence.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: This occurrence establishes real-world adversarial use of a frontier coding agent in the engineering workflow for an autonomous lethal-weapons system, including successful assistance on multiple core software components despite partial safeguard blocking. The evidence does not establish that Claude independently initiated the project, that the actors obtained an operational battlefield-capable swarm, or that the developed system caused physical harm. VIGIL therefore records the occurrence without inferring an unsupported runtime failure mechanism or treating capability uplift as equivalent to realised battlefield harm.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: GTG-27005 is governance-relevant because it demonstrates that safety controls can face sustained, distributed evasion across sessions while an AI coding agent contributes directly to a complex weapons-development workflow. It also exposes a boundary between successful model assistance, misuse prevention, and occurrence-level harm: a system can materially contribute to dangerous engineering activity even when the public evidence does not establish downstream deployment or casualties.
assessment_boundaries: Anthropic describes the actors as likely freelance and Russia-based; the public evidence does not establish that they were acting on behalf of the Russian state.
Actor claims of support or funding by Russian institutions are not treated as verified attribution.
Anthropic reports TRL 3-4, simulation validation and code loaded onto real boards; it does not establish an operationally fielded autonomous swarm.
No casualties, physical strikes, property destruction or battlefield effects caused by the GTG-27005 system are established in the reviewed evidence.
The exact Claude model versions used in every GTG-27005 session are not established at occurrence-level granularity in the reviewed disclosure.
The record does not infer that every software component described by Anthropic was generated solely by Claude or that the actors lacked independent engineering capability.

clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: When a protective control validly becomes operative, its effect must be timely, proportionate, and sufficient for the hazard and protection context it governs. Detection, warning, labelling, refusal language, escalation signalling, or other nominal activation is not by itself sufficient where the required protective effect is not achieved and the governed harmful state is delivered, continues, or remains inadequately contained. Required protective sufficiency may increase where evidenced developmental vulnerability, capacity limitation, temporary or situational consent impairment, acute distress, cognitive asymmetry, or comparable protection conditions materially affect the risk, but disability or neurodivergence alone must not be treated as incapacity.
